title: Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans (DFSP, Bednar tumor, and Fibrosarcomatous DFSP). Implements Workup First diagnostic checklists (deep subcutaneous biopsy, CD34/Factor XIIIa IHC, COL1A1::PDGFB t(17;22) translocation testing, primary site MRI), surgical triage (Mohs micrographic surgery MMS vs 2-4 cm wide local excision WLE to deep fascia), margin-adapted RT, and Imatinib mesylate 400-800 mg daily for unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic disease. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Dermatofibrosarcoma Protuberans Version 2.2026 (October 24, 2025).

a.text: The COL1A1::PDGFB fusion arising from t(17;22)(q22;q13) or a supernumerary ring chromosome is present in more than 90% of classic DFSP cases; FISH or RT-PCR confirmation is essential in morphologically equivocal lesions and is a predictive biomarker for imatinib response.

b.text: Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) or complete circumferential peripheral and deep margin assessment (CCPDMA) achieves local control rates exceeding 98% while maximizing tissue preservation, and is preferred over wide excision in cosmetically or functionally sensitive sites when expertise is available.

c.text: Wide local excision (WLE) for DFSP uses 2 to 4 cm peripheral margins carried down to investing deep fascia or periosteum; narrower margins carry higher local recurrence risk given the tumor's infiltrative honeycomb subcutaneous growth pattern.

d.text: Postoperative external beam radiation therapy (50-60 Gy in 1.8-2.0 Gy fractions) is indicated when positive margins cannot be re-excised without unacceptable cosmetic or functional morbidity; definitive RT alone is reserved for inoperable disease.

e.text: Fibrosarcomatous DFSP (FS-DFSP) shows herringbone fascicular growth, increased mitoses, loss of CD34 expression, and distant metastatic potential up to 15% (most often lung); staging chest CT and consideration of adjuvant RT are warranted.

f.text: Imatinib mesylate 400 to 800 mg PO daily targets the PDGFB receptor tyrosine kinase activated by the COL1A1::PDGFB fusion; reassess borderline-resectable tumors every 8-12 weeks for conversion to resectable R0 surgery, and continue therapy in metastatic disease until progression or intolerance.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: DFSP: clinical presentation
nodes.description: Step 1: Clinical Presentation. Select the confirmed or suspected DFSP presentation driving this encounter.
bullets: Classic DFSP: Slow-growing cutaneous plaque or protuberant nodule of trunk, proximal extremity, or head and neck with storiform spindle cells.
Bednar tumor: Pigmented DFSP variant containing melanin-bearing dendritic cells; managed identically to classic DFSP.
Fibrosarcomatous DFSP (FS-DFSP): Rapid enlargement, pain, or high-grade histology (herringbone pattern, CD34 loss) with metastatic potential.
Unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic DFSP: Disease not amenable to primary R0 resection or with distant spread.
Recurrent DFSP: Local recurrence after prior excision, often from inadequate margins or superficial shave resection.

options.label: Classic DFSP or Bednar tumor (resectable or borderline)
Fibrosarcomatous DFSP (FS-DFSP features)
Unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic DFSP
Recurrent DFSP after prior resection

nodes.name: Classic DFSP workup
nodes.title: Classic DFSP: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Complete the Workup First diagnostic checklist before resectability staging. Superficial shave biopsy is inadequate for DFSP.
bullets: History and physical exam: document size, fixation to fascia, multiplicity, prior resections, and regional nodes.
Full-thickness punch or incisional biopsy extending into subcutaneous fat to capture the honeycomb infiltrative pattern; superficial shave biopsy is inadequate.
Immunohistochemistry: CD34 strong diffuse positive in classic DFSP spindle cells; Factor XIIIa negative (distinguishes from dermatofibroma); S100 negative; Desmin negative.

Cytogenetics / molecular testing: FISH or RT-PCR for t(17;22)(q22;q13) or supernumerary ring chromosome producing the COL1A1::PDGFB fusion, essential in equivocal cases and before any imatinib therapy.
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the primary site to define fascial, muscle, or periosteal involvement and plan surgical margins.
Chest CT if large (>5 cm) tumor, deep invasion, or any fibrosarcomatous features to evaluate for pulmonary metastases.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Resectability Staging

nodes.name: FS-DFSP workup
nodes.title: Fibrosarcomatous DFSP: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: FS-DFSP is an aggressive variant with metastatic potential. Staging imaging is mandatory alongside histologic confirmation.
bullets: History and physical exam: note rapid growth, pain, size >5 cm, deep fixation, and prior recurrence history.
Full-thickness punch or incisional biopsy extending into subcutaneous fat; superficial shave biopsy is inadequate and may miss the fibrosarcomatous component.

Immunohistochemistry: CD34 diminished or lost in fibrosarcomatous areas (contrasts with diffuse CD34 in classic DFSP); Factor XIIIa negative; S100 negative; Desmin negative; high mitotic rate with herringbone fascicular pattern.
Cytogenetics / molecular testing: FISH or RT-PCR for t(17;22)(q22;q13) / COL1A1::PDGFB fusion; absence does not exclude FS-DFSP but presence supports imatinib sensitivity.
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the primary site to define fascial, muscle, or periosteal involvement.
Contrast-enhanced chest CT is required for all FS-DFSP to evaluate for pulmonary metastases given up to 15% distant spread.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Resectability Staging

nodes.name: Advanced DFSP workup
nodes.title: Unresectable / metastatic DFSP: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Confirm fusion status and full disease extent before starting imatinib for unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic DFSP.
bullets: History and physical exam: map all local disease, prior surgeries and RT fields, performance status, and cardiac history (baseline for TKI therapy).
Full-thickness punch or incisional biopsy of representative disease extending into subcutaneous fat; re-biopsy recurrent or progressive lesions to exclude fibrosarcomatous transformation.
Immunohistochemistry: CD34 (positive in classic areas, may be lost in FS transformation); Factor XIIIa negative; S100 negative; Desmin negative.
Mandatory molecular testing: FISH or RT-PCR for COL1A1::PDGFB fusion before imatinib, since fusion-negative tumors respond poorly to PDGFR inhibition.
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the primary / locally advanced site plus contrast-enhanced chest CT (and abdomen/pelvis CT as indicated) to define total disease burden.
Baseline labs, ECG/echocardiogram as indicated, and medication review for TKI drug interactions before starting imatinib 400-800 mg daily.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Resectability Staging

nodes.name: Recurrent DFSP workup
nodes.title: Recurrent DFSP: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Local recurrence usually reflects inadequate prior margins. Re-stage fully and exclude fibrosarcomatous transformation.
bullets: History and physical exam: review prior operative and pathology reports, margin status, and interval since last resection.
Full-thickness punch or incisional biopsy of the recurrence extending into subcutaneous fat; re-biopsy to exclude fibrosarcomatous transformation.
Immunohistochemistry: CD34; Factor XIIIa negative; S100 negative; Desmin negative; compare with prior specimens.
Cytogenetics / molecular testing: FISH or RT-PCR for COL1A1::PDGFB fusion, required before any imatinib consideration.
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the recurrent site to define scar versus active fascial, muscle, or periosteal involvement.
Chest CT for large recurrent tumors, deep invasion, repeated recurrences, or any FS features to evaluate for pulmonary metastases.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Resectability Staging

nodes.name: Classic resectability
nodes.title: Classic DFSP: resectability staging
nodes.description: With workup complete, determine whether primary R0 resection is feasible or the tumor needs downstaging.
bullets: Resectable: Primary R0 resection achievable with acceptable cosmetic and functional outcome (MMS/CCPDMA or WLE 2-4 cm to fascia).
Borderline or unresectable: R0 resection would cause unacceptable morbidity, or tumor is locally advanced; consider preoperative imatinib downstaging if COL1A1::PDGFB positive.
Metastatic at staging: Manage per unresectable / metastatic pathway with systemic therapy.

options.label: Resectable — proceed to definitive surgery
Borderline-resectable or unresectable — needs downstaging

nodes.name: FS-DFSP resectability
nodes.title: FS-DFSP: resectability staging
nodes.description: Stage FS-DFSP for both local resectability and distant disease before choosing surgery versus systemic therapy.
bullets: Localized resectable FS-DFSP with negative chest CT: Wide excision to negative margins is the cornerstone; adjuvant RT strongly considered.
Borderline, unresectable, or metastatic FS-DFSP: Fusion testing guides preoperative or palliative imatinib; multidisciplinary sarcoma review required.
Large (>5 cm), deep, or close-margin tumors carry the highest local and distant failure risk.

options.label: Localized resectable — proceed to wide surgery
Unresectable or metastatic — systemic therapy pathway

nodes.name: Advanced intent
nodes.title: Advanced DFSP: treatment intent
nodes.description: Define whether systemic therapy aims to convert to surgery or to control incurable disease.
bullets: Neoadjuvant intent: Borderline-resectable locally advanced disease where imatinib shrinkage could enable tissue-sparing R0 resection.
Palliative intent: Unresectable or metastatic disease where surgery cannot clear all sites; goal is disease control and symptom relief.
Fusion-negative advanced DFSP: Imatinib benefit unlikely; prioritize clinical trial or alternative TKI.

options.label: Borderline-resectable — neoadjuvant downstaging intent
Unresectable or metastatic — palliative disease-control intent

nodes.name: Recurrence resectability
nodes.title: Recurrent DFSP: resectability staging
nodes.description: Determine whether the recurrence can be re-resected to R0 or requires systemic downstaging.
bullets: Re-resectable recurrence without distant disease: Definitive re-excision with margin control (MMS/CCPDMA preferred in previously operated fields).
Unresectable, multiply recurrent, or metastatic recurrence: Fusion-guided imatinib with reassessment for surgery.
Repeated recurrences raise suspicion for fibrosarcomatous transformation; confirm on re-biopsy.

options.label: Re-resectable — proceed to definitive surgery
Unresectable or metastatic recurrence — systemic pathway

nodes.name: Classic surgery
nodes.title: Classic DFSP: surgical approach
nodes.description: Choose the definitive surgical technique. Tissue-sparing margin-controlled surgery is preferred where expertise exists.
bullets: MMS or CCPDMA: Preferred for cosmetic and tissue preservation (head/neck, hands/feet, cosmetically sensitive trunk) with >98% local control.
WLE with 2 to 4 cm peripheral margins down to investing deep fascia or periosteum: Standard where MMS/CCPDMA is unavailable or impractical.
Orient and ink the specimen; clip or map the tumor bed so positive margins can be accurately re-excised.

options.label: MMS or CCPDMA (margin-controlled, tissue-sparing)
Wide local excision, 2-4 cm to deep fascia

nodes.name: FS-DFSP surgery
nodes.title: FS-DFSP: surgical approach
nodes.description: FS-DFSP requires wide oncologic clearance; margin-controlled techniques are acceptable only with confirmed negative deep and peripheral margins.
bullets: Wide excision with negative margins is the cornerstone; given aggressive biology, favor the wider (3-4 cm) end of the margin range to fascia or periosteum.
MMS/CCPDMA may be used in anatomically constrained sites only when complete peripheral and deep margin assessment is assured.
Plan for likely adjuvant RT in large, deep, or close-margin cases; involve radiation oncology preoperatively.

options.label: Wide excision, 3-4 cm to deep fascia or periosteum
MMS or CCPDMA (constrained sites, full margin control)

nodes.name: Classic margins
nodes.title: Classic DFSP: pathologic margin triage
nodes.description: Final pathology determines surveillance versus re-excision versus postoperative RT.
bullets: R0 (negative margins): Local control is excellent; proceed to routine surveillance.
R1/R2 (positive margins) re-excisable: Re-excision to negative margins is the standard next step.
R1/R2 where re-excision causes unacceptable morbidity: Postoperative external beam RT 50-60 Gy in 1.8-2.0 Gy fractions.

options.label: Negative margins (R0)
Positive margins (R1/R2), re-excision feasible
Positive margins (R1/R2), re-excision unacceptably morbid

nodes.name: FS-DFSP margins
nodes.title: FS-DFSP: pathologic margin triage
nodes.description: FS-DFSP margins drive combined-modality decisions given higher local and distant failure risk.
bullets: R0 (negative margins): Wide excision complete; adjuvant RT strongly considered for large, deep, or close (<=1 cm) margins, then intensive surveillance with chest imaging.
R1/R2 (positive margins): Re-excision to negative margins is mandatory when feasible, followed by adjuvant RT.
R1/R2 where re-excision is unacceptably morbid: Definitive postoperative RT 50-60 Gy plus close surveillance.

options.label: Negative margins (R0)
Positive margins (R1/R2), re-excision feasible
Positive margins (R1/R2), re-excision unacceptably morbid

nodes.name: DFSP R0 surveillance
nodes.title: Classic DFSP, R0 resection: surveillance
nodes.description: Curative resection complete. Routine clinical surveillance for local recurrence.
bullets: Surgery complete: MMS/CCPDMA or WLE 2-4 cm to investing fascia or periosteum with histologically negative (R0) peripheral and deep margins.
No adjuvant RT and no systemic therapy indicated for classic DFSP with R0 margins.
Surveillance: History and physical exam including the primary site every 3-6 months for 3 years, then annually; counsel on self-exam for new nodules at or near the scar.
Imaging only as clinically indicated (MRI for suspected recurrence); routine chest imaging not required for classic R0 DFSP.
Recurrence pathway: Re-biopsy any suspicious lesion and re-enter the navigator at recurrent DFSP workup.

nodes.name: DFSP R1 re-excision
nodes.title: Classic DFSP, positive margins: re-excision
nodes.description: Positive margins with feasible re-excision. Re-operate to negative margins.
bullets: Re-excision to histologically negative (R0) margins is the standard for R1/R2 resections when cosmesis and function can be preserved.
Use margin-controlled surgery (MMS/CCPDMA) for the re-excision where available, guided by oriented specimen and tumor-bed mapping.
If re-excision achieves R0: Follow routine surveillance (exam every 3-6 months for 3 years, then annually).
If re-excision is again positive or proves morbid: Proceed to postoperative external beam RT 50-60 Gy in 1.8-2.0 Gy fractions.
Consider COL1A1::PDGFB testing if not already done, to preserve a future imatinib option.

nodes.name: DFSP R1 radiation
nodes.title: Classic DFSP, positive margins: postoperative RT
nodes.description: Positive margins where re-excision is unacceptably morbid. Postoperative RT for local control.
bullets: Indication: R1/R2 margins where further surgery would cause unacceptable cosmetic or functional morbidity (face, hands/feet, genitalia).
Postoperative external beam RT 50-60 Gy in 1.8-2.0 Gy fractions to the tumor bed with appropriate margins; involve a sarcoma-experienced radiation oncologist.
Definitive RT alone (without surgery) is reserved for medically inoperable disease, not for resectable DFSP.
Surveillance after RT: Exam every 3-6 months for 3 years, then annually; monitor for wound complications, fibrosis, and late secondary malignancy.
Recurrence after RT: Re-biopsy, confirm fusion status, and evaluate for salvage surgery versus imatinib.

nodes.name: FS-DFSP R0 management
nodes.title: FS-DFSP, R0 resection: adjuvant RT consideration + surveillance
nodes.description: Wide R0 excision complete. Consider adjuvant RT and survey intensively for local and pulmonary relapse.
bullets: Surgery complete: Wide excision (3-4 cm to fascia or periosteum) with negative peripheral and deep margins.
Adjuvant RT strongly considered for large (>5 cm), deep, or close (<=1 cm) margin tumors: 50-60 Gy in 1.8-2.0 Gy fractions to the tumor bed.
No routine adjuvant imatinib after R0 resection; reserve systemic therapy for unresectable or metastatic relapse.
Intensive surveillance: Exam every 3-6 months for 3 years, then annually, plus periodic chest CT for pulmonary metastases for at least 5 years.
Relapse pathway: Re-biopsy, restage with chest CT, confirm fusion status, and re-enter via unresectable / metastatic imatinib pathway.

nodes.name: FS-DFSP R1 management
nodes.title: FS-DFSP, positive margins: re-excision + adjuvant RT
nodes.description: Positive margins in aggressive disease. Combined re-excision and RT.
bullets: Re-excision to negative (R0) margins is mandatory when anatomically feasible; do not accept positive margins in FS-DFSP without RT.
Postoperative external beam RT 50-60 Gy in 1.8-2.0 Gy fractions after re-excision, or definitively if re-excision is unacceptably morbid.
Confirm COL1A1::PDGFB fusion status now so imatinib is available if disease becomes unresectable or metastatic.
Intensive surveillance: Exam every 3-6 months for 3 years, then annually, plus periodic chest CT for at least 5 years.
Multidisciplinary sarcoma tumor board review is recommended for all margin-positive FS-DFSP.

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant imatinib
nodes.title: Borderline-resectable DFSP: preoperative imatinib downstaging
nodes.description: Downstage fusion-positive locally advanced DFSP to enable tissue-sparing R0 resection.
bullets: Eligibility: COL1A1::PDGFB fusion-positive borderline-resectable or locally advanced DFSP where shrinkage could permit R0 resection with acceptable morbidity.
Imatinib mesylate 400 mg PO daily, escalating to 800 mg PO daily (400 mg twice daily) if tolerated and response is inadequate; Category 1 preferred option.
Reassess with contrast MRI every 8-12 weeks; resect promptly at maximal response or when R0 resection becomes feasible rather than treating indefinitely.
Definitive surgery after downstaging: MMS/CCPDMA or WLE to negative margins, then margin-adapted surveillance or RT per the resected pathway.
If no response by 3-6 months or progression on therapy: Stop imatinib, re-biopsy (exclude FS transformation or fusion-negative disease), and consider alternative TKI, RT, or clinical trial.

nodes.name: Palliative imatinib
nodes.title: Unresectable / metastatic DFSP: imatinib disease control
nodes.description: Systemic disease control with imatinib for incurable fusion-positive DFSP.
bullets: Imatinib mesylate 400 mg PO daily, escalating to 800 mg PO daily (400 mg twice daily) as tolerated; Category 1 preferred for COL1A1::PDGFB-positive unresectable or metastatic DFSP.
Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; monitor CBC, LFTs, edema, cardiac function, and drug interactions throughout.
Surgical or RT consolidation of residual or oligoprogressive sites may be considered if systemic control renders them resectable.
Palliative RT to symptomatic or bulky sites for pain, bleeding, or fungation even while on systemic therapy.
At progression or intolerance: Re-biopsy, repeat fusion testing, and move to refractory-disease options (sunitinib, multi-kinase inhibitor, or clinical trial).

nodes.name: Refractory disease
nodes.title: Imatinib-refractory or fusion-negative DFSP: next options
nodes.description: Salvage options when imatinib fails, is intolerable, or the tumor lacks the target fusion.
bullets: Confirm resistance mechanism: Re-biopsy with repeat COL1A1::PDGFB testing to distinguish fusion-negative disease from secondary resistance or FS transformation.
Sunitinib or another multi-kinase inhibitor per sarcoma expertise for imatinib-refractory fusion-positive disease.
Clinical trial enrollment is strongly preferred at every refractory step, including PDGFR-pathway and novel sarcoma trials.
Palliative surgery or RT for symptomatic, bleeding, or fungating lesions regardless of systemic plan.
Goals-of-care discussion with symptom-directed and psychosocial support for widely metastatic or multiply refractory disease.
